Class RowsManager

java.lang.Object
model.rowsManager.RowsManager
public class RowsManager extends Object
Manages the four card rows that form the central board offer, together with the underlying decks and event resolution logic.

The board is organised into two parallel offer tracks:

  • Tribe track — a top row and a bottom row of TribeCards drawn from a single TribeDeck.
  • Building track — a top row and a bottom row of BuildingCards. Cards progress across three era-specific BuildingDecks: Era I fill the top row at setup, and each era transition promotes the current top row to the bottom and loads the next era deck into the top.

Event cards embedded in the tribe rows are resolved through a dedicated EventResolver.

The typical lifecycle of this class across a game is:

  1. setup(int) — called once during SetupPhase to initialise decks and populate the starting rows.
  2. resolveEvents(List) — called each round by EndOfRoundPhase to resolve events in the bottom tribe row.
  3. endRound(int) — called each round to rotate tribe rows.
  4. changeEra() — called when the era advances to rotate building rows and load the next era deck.
  5. resolveAllEvents(List) — called once by EndOfGamePhase to resolve all remaining events on the board.

  • Method Details

    • setup

      public void setup(int playerCount)
      Initializes all decks and populates the starting rows (Setup, steps 3–6).

      1. Creates all cards via the factories;

      2. Initializes each deck (filtering by playerCount, shuffling, selecting);

      3. Draws the bottom row: playerCount + 1 tribe cards;

      4. Draws the top row: playerCount + 4 tribe cards;

      5. Places all Era I building cards face up in the top row.

      Parameters:
      playerCount - number of players in the game (2–5)

    • resolveEvents

      public List<EventResolutionDto> resolveEvents(List<Player> players)
      This method is responsible for resolving the events present in the bottom row at the end of the round, it is called by the EndOfRoundPhaseHandler at first it collects all the EventCard in the bottom row. The EventResolver sorts events by type and era, then it calls the resolve method of each EventCard, passing the list of players as parameter, so that the EventCard can apply its effect on the players.

    • resolveAllEvents

      public List<EventResolutionDto> resolveAllEvents(List<Player> players)
      Solves all the events on the board. Called only by EndOfGamePhase EventResolver sorts events by era and type, moving sustenance event at the end of the list from all cards present on the board. Then resolves all the events
      NOTE: to create the list of all cards present on the board it puts bottomRow cards first because maybe there could be some ERA_II card

    • endRound

      public void endRound(int playerCount)
      1. discard all tribe cards from bottom row 2. moves all tribe cards from top row to bottom row 3. restores top row tribe cards, drawing from tribe deck
      Parameters:
      playerCount - the number of players (used to determine how many cards to draw)

    • changeEra

      public void changeEra()
      1. discard all building cards from bottom row 2. moves all building cards from top row to bottom row 3. restores top row building cards, drawing from next era building deck

    • removeCard

      public void removeCard(int cardId)
      Removes a card by its unique identifier from all four rows. Searches through all tribe and building rows (top and bottom) and removes the first card matching the given ID. Does nothing if no card with the specified ID is found.
      Parameters:
      cardId - the unique identifier of the card to remove

    • getAllTribeCardsOnBoard

      public List<TribeCard> getAllTribeCardsOnBoard()
      Returns all tribe cards currently on the board (top and bottom rows). The returned list contains bottom row cards first, followed by top row cards.
      Returns:
      a List of all TribeCards present on the board

    • getAllCardsOnBoard

      public List<Card> getAllCardsOnBoard()
      Returns all cards (tribe and building) currently on the board (top and bottom rows). The returned list contains cards in the following order: bottom tribe row, top tribe row, bottom building row, top building row.
      Returns:
      a List of all Cards present on the board
